assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I think you should go with Policy 1. Thats the one where we can bring our phones to school and use them at lunch and free periods, but they have to be off during class.

My first reason is safety. Alot of kids walk home or ride the bus, and some of us stay after for practice. Sometimes plans change and our parents need to get ahold of us. One time last year my ride forgot to pick me up and I couldn't even call my mom. A phone sitting at home doesn't help with that at all.

Another reason is that Policy 1 teaches us to be responsible. We need to learn when to put our phones away, because someday we will have jobs and have to do it there too. If you just ban phones then we never learn that.

Also Policy 2 would be really hard to do. Teachers would have to check backpacks instead of teaching, and kids would probably just hide there phones anyway.

Please give us a chance to show you we can be trusted.

Sincerely,
A Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I think you should pick Policy 1. It lets students bring phones to school and use them at lunch and free periods, as long as they are off in class.

My first reason is safety. A lot of us walk home, ride the bus, or stay late for practice. Plans change, and it is good when parents can reach us. Some people say the office phone works fine. It is not much help when the office closes at five.

My second reason is responsibility. We will have phones at every job, so it is smart to learn now when to put them away. Policy 2 just moves that lesson to later.

Also, Policy 2 would not be easy to enforce. Teachers would have to check backpacks, and kids would hide phones anyway. That is really unfair to teachers.

Policy 1 keeps class time safe for learning and gives us free time to use phones. Students who do not follow the rule should hand over the phone for the day.

Sincerely,
A Student
